classification.difficultyReason: Eliminate time using the supplied equations, rearrange into the specified quadratic and substitute target coordinates to calculate two angles.

content.prompt:
A gun fires a shell with constant initial speed $V$ and variable angle of elevation $\alpha$.

The displacements after $t$ seconds are $x=Vt\cos\alpha$ and $y=-\frac12gt^2+Vt\sin\alpha$.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Show that the Cartesian equation may be written as
$$gx^2\tan^2\alpha-2xV^2\tan\alpha+(2yV^2+gx^2)=0.$$

answer.worked:
From $x=Vt\cos\alpha$,
$$t=\frac{x}{V\cos\alpha}.$$
Substitute into $y$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=-\frac g2\left(\frac{x}{V\cos\alpha}\right)^2+\frac{Vx\sin\alpha}{V\cos\alpha}\\y&=x\tan\alpha-\frac{gx^2\sec^2\alpha}{2V^2}.\end{aligned}$$
Use $\sec^2\alpha=1+\tan^2\alpha$ and rearrange:
$$\frac{gx^2}{2V^2}(1+\tan^2\alpha)-x\tan\alpha+y=0.$$
Multiply by $2V^2$:
$$gx^2\tan^2\alpha-2xV^2\tan\alpha+(2yV^2+gx^2)=0.$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Suppose $V=200\text{ m/s}$ and the shell hits a target $3\text{ km}$ horizontally and $0.5\text{ km}$ vertically from the gun. Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^2$. Show that $\tan\alpha=\frac{4+\sqrt3}{3}$ or $\tan\alpha=\frac{4-\sqrt3}{3}$, and hence find the two possible values of $\alpha$ to the nearest minute.

answer.worked:
Use $V=200$, $x=3000$, $y=500$ and $g=10$, in SI units:
$$\begin{aligned}10(9\times10^6)\tan^2\alpha&-2(3000)(4\times10^4)\tan\alpha\\&+\bigl(2(500)(4\times10^4)+9\times10^7\bigr)=0.\end{aligned}$$
Simplify:
$$\begin{aligned}9\tan^2\alpha-24\tan\alpha+13&=0,\\\tan\alpha&=\frac{24\pm\sqrt{576-468}}{18},\\\tan\alpha&=\frac{24\pm6\sqrt3}{18},\\\tan\alpha&=\frac{4\pm\sqrt3}{3}.\end{aligned}$$
The two angles of elevation are
$$\begin{aligned}\alpha&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4+\sqrt3}{3}\right)\approx62^\circ22',\\\alpha&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{4-\sqrt3}{3}\right)\approx37^\circ05'.\end{aligned}$$
